:::{#thm-square-of-a-sum}
#### Square of a sum

For any numbers $a$ and $b$,

$$
(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2
$$

:::

::: proof
By @sol-square-of-a-sum.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-square-of-a-difference}
#### Square of a difference

Replacing $b$ by $-b$ in @thm-square-of-a-sum
gives $(a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2$.
For example, the square $(y - \hy)^2$
of the difference between an observed value $y$ and a prediction $\hy$ of it
expands this way.
With $y = 5$ and $\hy = 3$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
(5 - 3)^2 &= 2^2 \\
&= 4,
\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}
5^2 - 2 \cdot 5 \cdot 3 + 3^2 &= 25 - 30 + 9 \\
&= 4.
\end{aligned}
$$

:::
